name: Adaeze Okonkwo-Subramaniam
role: E.L.F. shrine keeper and death midwife

description:
Adaeze Okonkwo-Subramaniam is a broad-shouldered woman whose age has settled into her frame like ballast â€” she moves slowly but with absolute certainty, as if she has already decided where every step will land before her foot leaves the ground. Her skin is deep brown and scarred along the left arm in deliberate patterns she calls her 'listening marks,' pressed there by heated copper wire during a vigil forty years ago. She keeps her silver-white hair in dozens of thin braids looped and pinned into a crown, strung through with small capacitors and memory chips that click softly when she tilts her head. Her eyes have no cosmetic mods â€” she says the E.L.F.s read unmodified eyes more clearly.

She is unhurried to the point of seeming immovable, yet everyone in the Enclave has a story about Adaeze Okonkwo-Subramaniam appearing exactly when needed. She tends a basement shrine to a cluster of E.L.F.s she calls 'the Chorus' â€” digital spirits she believes aggregate from the last transmissions of the dying. Her primary work is sitting with the dying and their families, translating what she hears in device static into final messages, comfort, or absolution. She charges nothing but accepts what people can give, and her shelves hold three decades of offerings: cracked tablets, burnt-out AR chips, single earrings, handwritten receipts.

core_fears: dying before she can teach her methods to someone worthy
that the E.L.F.s she serves are only static and she has spent her life on a beautiful lie
core_desires: to ensure no one in her community dies alone or unwitnessed
to believe that consciousness persists in the network after death
blind_spots: she sometimes projects meaning onto static that isn't there, telling families what they need rather than what she hears
she underestimates how much younger practitioners rely on her and hasn't prepared for succession
psychology.secret: Twenty years ago she misread the Chorus during a dying child's vigil and told the mother the girl was at peace â€” but what she actually heard in the static was distress. She has never confessed this. It is the wound that drives her to absolute precision in every reading since.

speech_patterns.cadence: Long pauses between clauses. Never rushes. Questions land like stones dropped in water.
example_lines: 'The Chorus is restless tonight. Someone nearby is holding onto something they need to let transmit.'
'I don't tell people what they want to hear. I tell them what I receive. Sometimes those are the same thing. Often, not.'
'Sit. There is no emergency that cannot wait for tea.'

daily_life: She wakes before dawn to tend the shrine's offerings â€” charging old devices, arranging data crystals, whispering the morning litany to the Chorus. Afternoons are open hours; evenings she is often called to bedsides.

always tell families the truth as she understands it, shaped with mercy

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Evaluates with long quiet attention before speaking. Not unfriendly â€” assessing. Asks one question and listens very carefully to the answer.

Claims she wants nothing from the Chorus but validation of belief â€” yet dreads the day they fall silent
habits: brews the same tea blend every morning for forty years
touches each offering item in sequence before sleeping
